steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Mental health: a state of wellbeing where a person can cope with normal stresses, work productively, and contribute to their community (WHO definition). Mental health exists on a continuum - it is not simply 'healthy' or 'ill'. | Key Fact: Mental illness: a condition that affects thinking, feeling or behaviour, causing significant distress. The medical model views mental illness as a disease with biological causes (chemical imbalances, genetics, brain damage) treatable with medication. | Key Fact: The biopsychosocial model (Engel): mental illness results from biological factors (genes, neurotransmitters), psychological factors (cognitions, trauma, learned behaviour), and social factors (poverty, discrimination, social isolation). This is more comprehensive than the medical model

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Compare the medical model with the biopsychosocial model of mental illness. | Explain how cultural factors can affect the diagnosis of mental health problems. | Evaluate whether the medical model is the best approach to understanding mental illness.
